title: RAQEB: Security Architecture for the Road-Side Units of the Internet of Vehicles Using Post-Quantum Techniques, Trust Scores, and Hash Chains
content: The Internet of Vehicles (IoV) requires constant exchange of telemetry data between vehicles and roadside units (RSUs). The traditional key exchange and digital signature algorithms based on RSA and elliptic curve cryptography are vulnerable to quantum computer attack and make all vehicular long-term communications retrospectively decryptable and forgeable. In this paper, we propose RAQEB, a post-quantum roadside unit security architecture which exploits post-quantum cryptographic standardization, trust-aware edge enforcement, tamper-evident auditing, and real-time security monitoring. A vehicle simulator encrypts a session key with ML-KEM-768, derives an AES-GCM key from SHAKE256 hash of the key, and signs a message with ML-DSA-87. An RSU, implemented on a Raspberry Pi board, verifies a message signature, prevents replay attack by refusing to accept any nonces that were used earlier, detects anomalies by analyzing speed, GPS position, and flooding rules, maintains a dynamically changing trust score of each vehicle, quarantines vehicles with low trust score, records security events in the hash-chained audit log, and reports them to the Splunk Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) dashboard. While existing IoV security systems address either authentication, anomaly detection, or auditability separately, RAQEB combines these security properties into one roadside unit-centric process. ProVerif model of the protocol proves its session key secrecy and origin authentication properties against the Dolev-Yao attacker. Experimental validation of the security behavior of RAQEB includes seven scenarios such as normal operation, replay attack, invalid signature, GPS spoofing, speed anomaly, flooding, and low-trust quarantine. The prototype can process about 25 messages/s with 25% CPU utilization and 150 MB RAM consumption. Experiments are done using a laptop-based vehicle simulator and one RSU on a local network; hence, scalability, detection accuracy, and field application of RAQEB is left for future research.
